notice: All organizations, inputs, activity and results are synthetic. This proposed workflow is not a connected employer system or measured company performance.
title: Model the partner journey before automating the next step.
intro: A proposed systems workbench for Grow Therapy’s EAP motion: connect benefits consultants and employers with clear entity relationships, data ownership and tested handoffs.
queueIntro: Fictional organization-level partner and employer records only. No employee health details, patient referrals, clinical decisions or provider eligibility are included.
workbenchIntro: Review the commercial relationship graph and staging checks. This concept supports an employer-benefits sales process; it does not determine anyone’s care or coverage.
firstBody: Define the organization model and allowed stages, validate duplicate and missing-owner cases, and make both relationship owners visible before automation.

fields.label: Consultant, employer and parent relationships mapped
Field definitions and source ownership agreed
Data access limited to organization-level context
Workflow validated in a staging scenario
Consultant and employer next-action owners assigned

rules.title: Resolve the partner relationship graph
rules.next: Keep a benefits consultant, employer and parent distinct before linking an opportunity.

rules.title: Keep the commercial motion explicit
rules.next: This pilot covers organization-level EAP evaluation, not patient referral triage or provider credentialing.

rules.title: Define the data contract
rules.next: Document organization keys, allowed stages and authoritative owners before adding automation.

rules.title: Review the data boundary
rules.next: Do not place employee health, patient or provider credentialing data in this commercial research workflow.

rules.title: Validate the proposed logic first
rules.next: Check duplicate relationships, missing owners and failed syncs before proposing production rollout.

rules.title: Assign both sides of the partner handoff
rules.next: Clarify who owns the consultant relationship and who receives the employer evaluation.

ready.title: Ready for an EAP architecture review
ready.next: The GTM architecture lead can inspect the relationship model, data contract and staging evidence before approving any production scope.

experiments.name: Relationship-aware partner routing
experiments.hypothesis: An explicit consultant-to-employer link reduces lost ownership.
experiments.treatment: Relationship graph and separate next-action owners
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

experiments.name: Staging before rollout
experiments.hypothesis: Testing failure cases improves integration reliability.
experiments.primary: Correct outcomes across agreed test cases
experiments.guardrail: Untested production changes and silent failures
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

roadmap.title: Define one commercial motion
roadmap.body: Partner with the GTM Engineering Lead on EAP entities, source ownership and the boundary between commercial and care data.

roadmap.title: Build and test in staging
roadmap.body: Implement a narrow partner handoff with duplicate handling, explicit exceptions and observable failures.
roadmap.measure: Correct scenario outcomes and owned exceptions

roadmap.title: Pilot with the commercial team
roadmap.body: Use feedback from consultant and employer owners to improve the workflow. Document monitoring and change review.
roadmap.measure: Accepted evaluations and reliable data movement

metricsTitle: Test the relationship model, not just the happy path.
metricsIntro: Synthetic staging cases for an organization-level EAP workflow.

rows: Preserve state and alert the owner

metricsNotes: This is a proposed acceptance checklist, not a report of Grow Therapy’s systems or clinical outcomes.
A commercial evaluation is not employee enrollment, care access, insurance coverage or a provider credentialing decision.
Production access and deployment would require the organization’s separate review and standards.
aiApplication: At Grow Therapy, I would apply MCP-assisted data inspection and coordinated research to the consultant-employer organization model. The loop would test duplicate, missing-owner and relationship-conflict cases before expanding the EAP handoff workflow.
